answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when a randomly sampled task is proven fraudulent through an auditable challenge. Splitting one operator across a thousand aliases does not create extra bonded value: each alias needs its own stake, and detection makes that capital unrecoverable. The harbor can host the challenge market, while a kernel enforces deadlines and a zephyr-like monitor flags suspicious clusters; the attacker pays both capital and time.
